Mood Board

1,220 sq ft · 2 bed / 3 bath

Style: Graphic Contemporary with a Color Accent. A black-and-white checkerboard floor and matte black hardware throughout carry the through-line, alongside clean-lined fixtures — Kohler Purist/Statement, the marble-and-matte-black-base dining table, the reeded vanity — chosen over anything rustic or ornate, with the living room's olive green sleeper sofa standing in as a deliberate pop of color rather than another neutral. The bathrooms extend that same high-contrast language: sea-glass ceramic, floor-to-ceiling in all three, grounded by the same black grout throughout — a small-format charcoal mosaic floor in the secondary and downstairs baths, solid Nero Marquina (matching the WIC and bedroom border) in the primary — that keep the rest of the house on-style. Practical, family-first choices are layered into that base: a stain-resistant sofa color, a corner sink chosen to fit a tight footprint. The kitchen's original farmhouse sink needs no exception made for it either — stripped of shiplap and open shelving, a plain apron-front basin is just a clean geometric shape, and it sits easily alongside the shaker doors and matte black hardware already there.

A black-and-white checkerboard floor, set on the diagonal, runs through the entire home — bedrooms, living room, kitchen, dining room, entryways, closets — at one consistent size throughout, stopping at the stairs (reclaimed wood treads), the primary bedroom's own 12" solid Nero border, and all three bathrooms, which take a solid-black or small-format charcoal mosaic floor instead (Nero Marquina, matching the primary bedroom's WIC and border, in the primary bath; charcoal mosaic in the secondary and downstairs baths), paired with sea-glass-look tiled walls and matte black hardware. Walk-in closets throughout get built-in cabinetry and organizer systems. The downstairs half bath is converted into a full bath laid out as a curbless wet room.

A note on flexibility. The one must-have is the checkerboard tile throughout. Everything else — colors, materials, fixtures, and how to get the best value — is genuinely open to the design firm's judgment. This is a starting reference, not a locked spec. The general aesthetic direction we're after: fresh and current, the kind of space that photographs well today, but grounded enough in timeless choices that it won't read as dated in five or ten years.

Bathrooms

Six wall tile options compared for the three bathrooms — on reflectance, price, format, and how each pairs with the bathroom floor: Dawson, Charcoal, a near-neutral dark gray at 30.4% reflectance and 5.6% saturation, still the floor in the secondary and downstairs bathrooms (the primary bathroom switched to solid Nero Marquina, 16% reflectance, on 2026-09-03 — see the Primary Bathroom section). Leona's checkerboard values (≈85% white, ≈16% black, both warm) are marked on the chart for reference alongside Dawson. Lilah, Opal is the preferred look, specified throughout this book.

Transitions

Where two preferred materials physically meet in the plan. Walls stack over floors, matching how they actually meet at the baseboard; two floors or two walls sit side by side instead, since neither reads as "on top" of the other.

Leona ↔ Dawson
Whole-house checkerboard meets the bathroom floor at each of the three bathroom thresholds.
Leona ↔ Hardwood
Checkerboard meets the black-stained hardwood where the stairs begin.
Gray Matters ↔ Hardwood
Tread nosing runs along the stairwell's painted wall.
Gray Matters ↔ Dawson
Bathroom floor meets the one wall left painted, the pocket-door wall, in each bath.
Lilah ↔ Dawson
Bathroom floor meets the floor-to-ceiling wall tile at the base of the tiled walls.
Lilah ↔ Gray Matters
The tiled wall meets the painted pocket-door wall at the inside corner, capped in a matte black edge profile.
Gray Matters ↔ Leona
Whole-house floor meets the painted wall at the baseboard line, in every room outside the bathrooms and stairs.
By Room
Primary Bedroom Primary Bathroom

Two twin beds on the north wall, each with a Thuma Pedestal Side Table and a canopy curtain divider between them. Checkerboard floor framed by a 12" solid Nero Marquina border, glossy gray walls, matte black hardware. West of the room: an open walk-in closet floored in the same solid Nero, then the primary bath beyond a pocket door.

Alcove tub/shower with a curved rod, matte black drain. Sea-glass ceramic wraps the tub and runs floor-to-ceiling down the vanity/toilet wall. Ceiling-mount rain head plus a matching handheld wand, same pairing as the other two baths. Single 36" Blonde vanity, matte black hardware. Solid Nero Marquina floor (switched from Charcoal mosaic 2026-09-03), gray walls, matte black fixtures, medicine cabinet.

Secondary Bedroom Secondary Bathroom

Checkerboard floor, glossy gray walls throughout, for easy wipe-down. Standalone furniture — platform bed, desk, and side table, all in oak finish. A reach-in closet with matte black hardware.

Shower-only, no tub — the whole room takes the same small-format charcoal mosaic floor with black grout as downstairs (the primary bath switched to solid Nero Marquina, 2026-09-03), with a linear drain in the shower matching downstairs. Paired with the same blue-green glossy ceramic on the walls, set in the same straight 6" grid with black grout, wrapping the shower and continuing along the full wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling. A frameless sliding glass door, matte black, closes the full 60" opening. Single 30" vanity, Blonde finish, matte black hardware. Gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, and a ceiling-mount rain head paired with a matching handheld wand.

Kitchen Dining Room Living Room Entryway Stairs

No changes to white kitchen cabinetry, stainless appliances, black granite countertop, or backsplash — shown here for flooring and wall color continuity, plus two counter stools at the island (the dining-room desk stations use low dining chairs instead, not stools — see below). New window treatment on the kitchen window. Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish, including the island's own west-facing cabinet face where the barstools pull up — full-height tile there was considered and descoped 2026-09-03 to control rising budget, so it stays painted like the rest of the room.

Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish. Kitchen cabinets and counters extend across the length of the dining room, dropped to table height with drawer-stack cabinetry at the two desk stations so they seat regular dining chairs instead of bar-height stools. The wall exposed behind each of the two knee-space gaps stays painted, same as the island's cabinet face above. Dining table is a 48" round dining table (white marble top, matte black base), seating six — 4 black ash dining chairs at the table, plus the 2 desk-station chairs available when guests need the extra seats. A matte black aluminum bi-fold door — three panels that fold away — opens the wall to the patio.

Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish for easy wipe-down. A power recline sleeper sofa provides additional guest space, centered in front of the built-in entertainment center. Built-in entertainment center remains, on the north wall east of the stairway opening and its pony wall.

An archway passageway wall between the living room and kitchen. Checkerboard floors, glossy gray walls. Optional: a shoe storage bench along the wall.

Connecting space between the living room and bedrooms upstairs. Reclaimed hardwood treads and risers, treads milled with a built-up roundover nose, both black-stained and finished in hard multi-coat polyurethane (matching a finish the owner already has and likes in another house). Walls gray, glossy finish. Handrail black-stained + polyurethane to match the treads; all other hardware in matte black.

Main floor plan — living room, entryway, stairs, kitchen, and dining room all drawn to scale (living room 171" x 169"; kitchen and dining room each 137" x 137"). Downstairs bath shown schematically; see its own detail plan.

Downstairs Bathroom Under-Stairs Closet

Half bath converted to a full bath: a curbless wet room, shower west of a fixed glass panel, toilet dry to the east. Opal tile floor-to-ceiling, black grout. Ceiling rain head paired with a matching handheld wand, corner sink with matching corner mirrors, the same Kingston toilet used elsewhere, and a 28" pocket door.

Next door: a wedge-shaped closet under the stair stringer, headroom tapering from 93" at the opening to 31" at the back. Oak shelving and a granite counter along the east wall, a clothes rod, a medicine cabinet, electrical outlets, and an over-mirror vanity light, with 6'6" of standing headroom over a 28"x21" floor space near the opening. No door — a ceiling-mount curtain screens the whole hallway pocket instead, hung just outside the jamb at the corridor's full 40" width. Checkerboard floor, matte black hardware.

Proposed floor plan to fit a full bath in place of the existing 1/2 bath. Room is 61" x 61", so the west wall bumps 6" into the entry beyond it to make 67" x 61".
